stemBlocks.value: A trapezium A with vertices (-5, 4), (-4, 4), (-3, 2) and (-5, 2) is drawn on a square grid. On the diagram, draw the image of A after it undergoes (i) a reflection in the line x = -1, labelled A', and (ii) a translation by the vector (4, -7), labelled A".
Think first: Both images come from the original trapezium A, not from each other, so go back to A's four vertices each time.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p261-q08 from workbook page 261.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the vertices of trapezium A from the grid.

contentBlocks.value: Top edge from (-5, 4) to (-4, 4); bottom edge from (-5, 2) to (-3, 2); the left side is vertical.

solutionSteps.instruction: For the reflection in x = -1, keep each y and send each x to -2 - x.

contentBlocks.value: The mirror is vertical, so the perpendicular distance to it is measured horizontally.

solutionSteps.instruction: Plot A' and check one vertex by counting squares.

contentBlocks.value: (-5, 4) is 4 squares left of x = -1, and (3, 4) is 4 squares right of it.
Result: A' drawn correctly on the right of the mirror line

solutionSteps.instruction: For the translation, apply 4 right and 7 down to the vertices of the original trapezium A.
Plot A" and join the vertices in the same order to complete the diagram.

contentBlocks.value: A" is the same way up as A; A' is a mirror image of A.
Result: Both images drawn and labelled

strategyBlocks.value: List the four vertices of A. For the reflection use (x, y) -> (-2 - x, y); for the translation use (x, y) -> (x + 4, y - 7). Plot each set of images and join them in the same order as the original.

whyThisWorks.value: Reflection and translation are both isometries: they preserve every length and angle, so each image is congruent to A. Reflection reverses orientation because points swap sides of the mirror line, while translation preserves orientation because every point moves by the same vector. Working vertex by vertex turns a drawing task into simple arithmetic.

commonErrors.misconception: Applying the translation to the reflected image A' instead of to the original A.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Applying the translation to the reflected image A' instead of to the original A.

commonErrors.misconception: Using x = -1 as the y-axis and reflecting to (5, 4).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using x = -1 as the y-axis and reflecting to (5, 4).

commonErrors.misconception: Mixing up the order of the components of the translation vector.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Mixing up the order of the components of the translation vector.

examTip.value: When a question says 'the image of A after it undergoes ...', every listed transformation starts from A unless the wording clearly says 'followed by'.
